subject: Social Media
title: Designing for Wellbeing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Designing for Wellbeing.

hook.text: What if apps were designed to make you happier instead of more engaged? The metrics would be different.

buildup.text: Some designers propose 'time well spent'—measuring quality of experience rather than quantity of use.

discovery.text: YouTube tested a 'satisfaction' metric alongside watch time. Satisfied users watched less but returned more.

twist.text: Shareholders resist. Less usage means fewer ads. Designing for wellbeing conflicts with revenue models.

climax.text: Until business models change, wellness features remain add-ons, not the foundation. The structure opposes health.

punchline.text: The solution isn't better features. It's better incentives.

quiz.question: What conflict prevents platforms from designing for wellbeing?
options: Less usage means fewer ads, conflicting with revenue
